title: The Federer template driving Rune's most emotional comeback match
text:
Rune Returns to Stockholm With Federer as His Blueprint

 Rune Takes Federer as His Blueprint for Stockholm Comeback 
 ATP Tour Rune Takes Federer as His Blueprint for Stockholm Comeback 
 Jim Flannigan | 10 November 2026 | 3 min read Holger Rune - Photo: IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Share this article
 Add us as a preferred source on Google 
 Holger Rune says Roger Federer’s famous 2017 comeback is the model for his own return from a ruptured Achilles. The Dane faces Zizou Bergs at the Stockholm Open on Tuesday, on the same court where his injury happened, in a key test of whether that blueprint can work for him.
 Rune looks to Federer for belief
 Speaking to Danish outlet SpilXperten before the tournament, Rune said he took Federer as an example. He explained that he thought back to what the Swiss achieved after returning from a knee injury around 2017, when he regained total dominance on the ATP Tour.
 For Rune, the comparison is about more than motivation. It gives him proof that a long layoff does not have to mark the end of a player’s best years. He spent almost 11 months on the sidelines, and when ATPTour.com asked what he was most proud of, he named his patience, his trust in the process and his resilience.
 He also admitted that coming back to Stockholm would feel “a bit overwhelming.” He was quick to add that the tournament was not to blame for his injury.
 What Federer achieved after his layoff
 Federer’s return remains one of the great stories in tennis. He had knee surgery in early 2016 and then shut down his season after Wimbledon that July. He came back in January 2017 at the age of 35, seeded 17th at the Australian Open, and beat Rafael Nadal in a five-set final to win the title.
 He went on to win Indian Wells, Miami and Wimbledon that year, taking the title at the All England Club without dropping a set. In February 2018 he returned to world number one at 36, becoming the oldest man to hold the top ranking.
 There are clear differences between the two cases. Federer was out for six months with a knee problem, while Rune has recovered from an Achilles rupture, one of the hardest injuries in sport to come back from. But Rune has youth on his side at 23.
 Federer during an exhibition in Tokyo last month – Photo: IMAGO/AFLOSPORT 
 Signs the comeback is on track
 Rune was ranked 11th and top seed in Stockholm last October when he ruptured his left Achilles while leading Ugo Humbert in the semifinals. He returns ranked 406th.
 His best result so far came at the Swiss Indoors in Basel last month. He beat Quentin Halys in a final-set tiebreak for his first ATP Tour win in 373 days. He then saved a match point against Hubert Hurkacz before winning 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 to reach the quarterfinals.
 A tough first step in Stockholm
 Bergs, the eighth seed and world number 44, will not make things easy. The Belgian beat Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6(4) in Shanghai in October, the biggest win of his career.
 Rune leads their head-to-head 2-0, though both matches came before his injury. He also has history on his side in Stockholm, where he won the title in 2022 by beating Stefanos Tsitsipas in the final.
 Stockholm is the last tournament of the season before the ATP Finals in Turin . Taylor Fritz is the top seed, and defending champion Casper Ruud is seeded second. Federer’s 2017 revival began with one good week in Melbourne. Rune will hope a strong run here, after his progress in Basel, can be the start of something similar.
 Written by
 Jim Flannigan
 Jim Flannigan is a tennis journalist and analyst. A competitive player until injury ended his playing career, he studied at the University of Leeds and has spent 16 years covering the sport as a freelancer. He writes primarily on Tenniswatcher.
